extracted.intended_audience: writers seeking literary representation (authors preparing elevator pitches)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on preparing a tight, well-rehearsed 30-second (elevator) pitch to impress literary agents in person or at events. Focuses on four essential components to include in a brief spoken pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevator pitch length and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared to pitch your idea in 30 seconds or fewer (this is called an 'Elevator Pitch'). Craft just a few key sentences and commit them to memory so you never waste an opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tight, well-rehearsed pitches are essential because agents have limited time. Practice so the pitch fits within ~30 seconds and can be delivered smoothly. The page promotes downloading the free guide 'Your 30-Second Pitch' for additional tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the literary agent who you are
rubrics_metrics.description: State your name and job title, or the title of the position you're seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: 'Hi, my name is Miranda Mechanic, and I’m a licensed automotive mechanic who writes how-to articles for women who don’t want their cars to get the best of them.' Keep this succinct and relevant to the project you're pitching.

rubrics_metrics.name: State what you want
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't beat around the bush — clearly state what you're after (e.g., placement, representation, or a specific opportunity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'I’m interested in placing some of my articles with your magazine, Auto Care for Everybody.' A direct, specific statement of intent helps the agent immediately understand your goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show why you're the best choice (relevant qualifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: List any degrees, writing credentials, training or experience that relate to what you're seeking; ensure the qualifications match your stated goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be brief and memorable; highlight the 'special something' that separates you from the crowd. If you lack directly related experience, name transferable qualities or skills (e.g., attention to detail, passion for the subject). Anti-pattern: listing credentials unrelated to the pitch (e.g., degrees in an unrelated field) which won't help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give a clear call to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask for what you want and provide a next step that leads to further interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'I’d like to show you copies of my articles, including “How to Change a Tire When It’s Twenty Below Zero” and “How to Add Oil When You’re Wearing a Power Suit.”' The call to action is essential — without it you may fail to convert the brief encounter into follow-up engagement.
